correctness.rationale: J_G(p)=p sum_v (1-p)^d follows exactly from singleton event. Put q=1-p; degree budget a_1=2(n-m)+sum_{d>=3}(d-2)a_d; derivative at q=1/2 nonnegative and at q=2/3 nonpositive with equality only 1- and 2-regular respectively. For q>=1/2, maximize each high-d second derivative coefficient d q^{d-2}((d-1)-(d+1)q) at q=(d-2)/(d+1), bounded strictly by 2(d-2), so F strictly concave on [1/2,1], proving unique peak and no other peak. Path/star limits, chorded cycle derivative 8/27 at q=2/3, and K13-plus-leaf four sign probes show sharp boundaries. Checked exact rational finite cases as corroboration.
